item.description: We are social beings by nature. We cannot isolate ourselves from others. We need each other. Sometimes it's good to be alone for mental health, but we shouldn't isolate ourselves for too long either; it's not good. Sergio L. Moreno Fuente: National Geographic.

item.title: Investigadores crean aeronaves ultraligeras para explorar una región casi desconocida de la Tierra. Su truco: surfear la luz del Sol
item.description: Entre la estratosfera y la termosfera se encuentra una franja en la que termina el alcance de los aviones y globos, pero también donde empieza el dominio de los satélites. Se trata de la mesosfera y, en su parte más alta a unos 70 km, hay una zona inexplorada que se ha apodado con humor científico como ignorosfera. Es extremadamente difícil de estudiar y el motivo es un problema físico. A esa altitud hay tan poco aire que un avión convencional o un globo no pueden mantenerse a flote, pero el aire restante es suficiente para frenar cualquier satélite y hacerlo caer. Sólo hemos podido medir a… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro Alcolea

item.title: China offers 15-year research grants to the world’s brightest young scientists
item.description: China is offering the world’s brightest young scientists generous 15-year research grants for free exploration, as the country accelerates its drive to become a global science powerhouse. Dou Xiankang, director of the National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC), the country’s top funder of basic research, told a recent academic forum that the agency was selecting a group of the brightest researchers under 35 for long-term financial backing. Once this group of exceptionally brilliant... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Dannie Peng

item.title: Galaxies in a cosmic house of mirrors
item.description: Image: This NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope Picture of the Month features galaxies in great detail that have been warped and multiplied like they’ve stepped into a house of mirrors. The brilliant golden galaxies splashed across this image belong to a galaxy cluster called MACS J0454.1-0300. The orange galaxies concentrated on one side of the cluster are not actually part of the cluster and are much farther away from us. MACS J0454.1-0300 is itself immensely distant: the light from these galaxies has been travelling to us for so long that we’re seeing the cluster as it was when the… Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: Getting AI 'drunk' makes it more likely to break rules, research finds
item.description: A study finds AI models are more likely to answer harmful questions or mishandle confidential information when told to act drunk. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
item.dc:creator: Cam Wilson

item.title: China ya sabe repostar satélites a 36.000 km de la Tierra. Lo preocupante es lo que puede hacer con esa capacidad
item.description: Quienes quieran avanzar en la carrera espacial deben hacer cuanto antes un check muy concreto en su lista de tareas conseguidas: repostar en órbita. Esto es necesario por muchos motivos , ya que es útil para alargar la vida de los satélites, pero también sirve para emprender viajes espaciales mucho más largos, tanto en tiempo como en distancia. Por eso es tan importante el nuevo gran hito de China: el repostaje de un satélite directamente en órbita terrestre alta (casi 36.000 km). Supuestamente, todo pasó el pasado mes de febrero , pero el país asiático no lo ha dado a conocer hasta ahora… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: AI identifies Senegal's smallholder crops 84% of the time using limited training data
item.description: Food in Senegal is mostly grown on small-scale, rain-dependent farms, leaving much of the population vulnerable to climate shocks, according to the World Food Programme. However, satellite crop-mapping technologies designed to monitor the impact of climate on farming are largely beyond the reach of the West African country. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Investigadores identificaron en Miramar una nueva especie de depredador que vivió hace unos 2,5 millones de años y habría pesado alrededor de 100 kilos. Fue denomina... Ver más

item.title: 55-million-year-old fossil bird shows how trogons evolved their unusual feet
item.description: A fossil of Daniatrogon kochi, discovered in Denmark, provides insights into the evolution of trogon feet. Researchers found that the trogons' unique foot morphology developed gradually over time. The fossil also shows changes in the shape of their beaks, which were narrower than those of modern species. Additionally, early trogoniforms displayed more varied beak and foot shapes, indicating a diverse ecology. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: SpaceX puts Starship megarocket in orbit for first time
item.description: The black-and-silver behemoth, standing more than 120 metres tall, rose through a thick cloud of smoke on an ambitious 14th test flight Publicado también por: Euronews. Fuente: The Hindu - International.

item.title: Saving the Siamese crocodile: Cambodia moves to protect one of the world’s last wild populations
item.description: Indigenous communities play crucial role, as ‘genetic bank’ area of wetland offers hope for critically endangered reptile In the 1990s, conservationists in Cambodia feared the Siamese crocodile had disappeared for good. Fishing and hunting had devastated the species throughout the 20th century, leaving populations across its native south-east Asia on the brink of extinction. But in villages dotted among the wetlands of the remote Cardamom mountains, Indigenous Chorng communities still reported seeing them. Passing this knowledge to researchers surveying the area in 2000 led to an official… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Pearce

item.title: Tracking researchers in Ukraine through war and armed conflict: The limits of free scholarly mobility
item.description: A study based on publication data traces how researchers moved within Ukraine and across borders between 2009 and 2022, with conflict-affected regions losing scholars while others became increasingly important destinations. These shifts were already underway after Russia illegally annexed Crimea and fighting began in the Donbas in 2014, underscoring that scholarly mobility during conflict cannot simply be understood as a matter of free choice. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Mars Has Its Charmes
item.description: Written by Athanasios (Thanos) Klidaras, Ph.D. candidate at Purdue University Sept. 21, 2026 After a long hiatus, the Perseverance rover updates page is back. A lot has happened on Mars in the meantime, and with regular updates now resuming, there is plenty to catch up on — Perseverance has been busy. The rover has spent […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Study across 40 countries: Political activism linked to representation
item.description: Not happy with the election result? Don't worry. Election Day is not the only opportunity to influence politics. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How Bolsonaro's statements destroyed the rainforest
item.description: Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro contributed to deforestation through statements opposing forest conservation, according to an international study led by the University of Bonn. The study found that destruction of the Amazon rainforest accelerated when Bolsonaro and his ministers posted messages opposing forest conservation on Twitter. Brazil's environmental authorities were greatly weakened during Bolsonaro's presidency, but the analysis suggests that even a perceived low risk of punishment was a driver of deforestation. The researchers estimate that the statements contributed to… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: In Japan, anti-foreigner fake news drives far-right gains
item.description: Japan risks being pulled into a spiral of online disinformation about foreign crime that is stoking xenophobia and playing into the hands of the far-right, researchers warn. The trend is reportedly deepening divisions within Japanese society and creating a feedback loop that experts say will be difficult to break. In August, Constella Security Japan, a Tokyo-based cybersecurity firm commissioned by the government to counter online disinformation, hosted a webinar for officials and media on fake... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Julian Ryall

item.title: When microbial DNA is scarce, new profiling method helps separate genuine signals from contamination
item.description: In acute, life-threatening infections, rapidly characterizing the microorganisms in a patient sample can help guide diagnosis and treatment. Computational methods known as taxonomic profilers can analyze metagenome sequencing data generated from the microorganisms' genomic information and compare it with reference genomes of individual microorganisms. However, taxonomic profilers are still under development and are not yet in common use. Current methods can produce false-positive results or inaccurate abundance estimates. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Fiery end for SpaceX Starship mission
item.description: Elon Musk’s SpaceX's next-generation Starship rocket reached orbit for the first time despite an engine shutdown. Fuente: Al Jazeera English.

item.title: Dopamine-based nanotubes combine heat, electrical stimulation and antioxidant release for first time
item.description: The research group at the Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia in Pontedera (Pisa), led by Gianni Ciofani, has developed new organic nanoparticles that combine multiple therapeutic functions in a single material for the first time. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Party leaders widening Washington's political chasm
item.description: Most of the polarization currently roiling Congress comes from political parties rather than individual politicians, a study co-authored by University of Miami Business School associate professor Chad Kendall finds. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Plasma treatment helps reveal how molecular coatings dope silicon
item.description: Controlling dopant concentration near the silicon surface is increasingly important for ultrashallow junctions and nanoscale devices. Mixed monolayer doping (MMLD) offers a surface-chemistry-based approach in which dopant-containing molecules are mixed with nondopant molecules to tune the amount of dopant available at the silicon surface before thermal diffusion. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Two-color glowing molecule could make wind tunnel tests more accurate
item.description: Most sensors can measure only one thing at a time, like a thermometer for temperature or a pressure gauge for pressure. Measuring two properties accurately from the same surface at the same moment usually means using two separate instruments—adding cost and complexity to the process. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Espionage boosted East Germany's economic output by 7.4%
item.description: East Germany's espionage activities in the West boosted the country's economic output by 7.4%. Value added in manufacturing alone increased by 22.3% through industrial espionage, equivalent to 20.2 billion East German marks or approximately 4.1 billion euros at 2020 prices. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hydrogen's distant glow opens new way to investigate dark energy
item.description: The Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME) has shown for the first time that it can detect the faint glow of hydrogen gas from deep in the universe's past using only its own data. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: October’s Night Sky Notes: Spooky Stargazing
item.description: The Ghoul Located within the constellation Perseus lies a star called Algol, also known as ‘Demon Star’ or ‘The Ghoul’. You can spot this star during the autumn months, along with Cassiopeia and Andromeda in the northeastern sky, beginning after 9 PM. In Greek mythology, this star represents the ‘blinking eye’ of the gorgon Medusa. […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: AI news coverage reveals hierarchy of innovators, regulators and overlooked regions
item.description: Analyzing more than 43,000 English-language newspaper articles, a new study reveals a highly stratified narrative about AI in which the news media allocate authority unequally, reinforcing the technology's prominent role in contemporary life. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Assembly pathway reveals how bacteria build protein coils that extend in acid
item.description: The assembly pathway behind refractile-body proteins may have finally been resolved, researchers from Science Tokyo report. Using genetic engineering and several techniques for analyzing protein structure, they investigated how four proteins work together to produce the correct architecture of these complex, pH-responsive protein machines, from the nanoscale to the microscale. The findings could help establish new frameworks for engineering dynamic protein systems as biotechnological tools. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Avian odysseys: Tracking raptor migrations from Europe to Africa
item.description: At the southwest tip of Sweden, the Falsterbo Peninsula stretches into the Baltic Sea, creating a natural bottleneck for hundreds of millions of birds traveling south for the winter each year. Falsterbo is particularly known for raptor migration. One autumn morning, I stood with a group of others by the lighthouse, watching birds gather to cross the open sea—a sight to take your breath away. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: European rivers are improving, but not fast enough to meet 2030 goals
item.description: The quality of European rivers has improved in recent years, but not at the pace required to meet the environmental targets set for 2030. This is one of the main conclusions of a study led by researchers María Pachés Giner and Remedios Martínez from the Institute of Water and Environmental Engineering at the Universitat Politècnica de València (UPV), published in Environmental Science and Pollution Research. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Experimental evidence of altermagnetism in a layered material opens a promising path toward future spintronics
item.description: To build the ultrafast computers of the future, scientists are looking beyond the electrical charge of electrons to another property: their spin. While conventional hardware relies on the movement of charge to process data, tapping into this intrinsic quantum property could enable researchers to reinvent how information travels through a circuit. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Exposed ends and bends attract DNA-cutting enzymes, live imaging reveals
item.description: Researchers at the Nano Life Science Institute (WPI-NanoLSI) at Kanazawa University have directly visualized how enzymes find and break DNA molecules in real time. Using high-speed atomic force microscopy, the team followed individual enzymes as they moved along DNA and found that they repeatedly returned to vulnerable regions before breaking them apart. The findings reveal how the structure of DNA influences its vulnerability to enzymatic breakdown. The research was led by Richard Wong and his team: Jingge Yang, Yujia Qiu, Keesiang Lim and Toshio Ando. The work is published in Nature… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Subjective and objective difficulty of English texts are related—but not the same
item.description: Evaluating the difficulty of English texts used in educational materials and language assessments is a central concern in English language education. Traditionally, researchers have relied on objective measures of text difficulty based on linguistic features, including characteristics of words and sentences. However, learners can differ substantially in how difficult they perceive the same text to be. To examine the relationship between objective and subjective text difficulty, the researchers investigated the extent to which objective estimates correspond with learners' perceptions. The work… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Meteor hit Oklahoma 100 million years later than previously thought
item.description: Researchers at The University of Texas at Austin have rewritten a small part of Oklahoma's geologic history with global implications for ancient life. Below the surface of the small town of Ames, Oklahoma, a meteor impact site spans miles. The crater is buried by sedimentary strata in the subsurface, but it remains an important marker of Oklahoma's ancient past and present-day economy; the Ames impact structure is a major oil and gas producer. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Uncovering species–specific chemical sensitivity by focusing on mammalian hormone receptor evolution
item.description: Chemicals affect biological species in different ways, posing a major challenge for assessing environmental chemical risks. However, the mechanisms behind these differences have remained largely unknown. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Mapping the 'social network' of proteins in the cell to understand how genes shape living things
item.description: One of biology's fundamental questions is how our genes shape who we are. Adrian Serohijos and Stephen Michnick, professors in the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Medicine at Université de Montréal's Faculty of Medicine, are studying the relationship between genotype and phenotype—that is, how DNA becomes RNA, then protein, and ultimately gives rise to observable characteristics in an individual or any other living organism. "We're trying to unravel the mechanisms of the genome, specifically how the information it encodes is processed inside the cell," Serohijos says. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Changing climate may influence risks from deadly rodent-borne diseases
item.description: Changes in rainfall can trigger increases in rodent populations and subsequent spikes in infection, new research has found, revealing how a changing climate could have consequences for human health. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Water-stable catalyst could bring carbon-bond chemistry closer to use in living cells
item.description: Olefin metathesis is one of the most important reactions in organic chemistry for forming carbon–carbon bonds—for example, in the production of pharmaceuticals, plastics and complex natural products. However, previous ruthenium catalysts that enable this reaction have faced a major challenge: They rapidly degrade in aqueous or biological environments, making their use in natural systems such as cells or blood extremely difficult. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ancient spearheads reveal how Ice Age humans learned the land
item.description: At the end of the last ice age, early humans crisscrossed the Americas following seasons, rivers and game, often with a trusty spear in hand. Nearly 13,000 years later, archaeologists are using those spearheads to study how America's first inhabitants understood risk. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hibernating bacteria can invade hospitals and survive outer space—but their energy budget reveals a weakness
item.description: A spore is a bacterium's survival capsule: dried almost solid and wrapped in protein armor, with its chemical processes shut down. Bacteria enter this state of hibernation when environmental conditions are unfavorable. What's left is close to indestructible: It can survive boiling, desiccation, radiation and the vacuum of space. NASA once bolted Bacillus spores to the outside of a satellite and left them in orbit for nearly six years; the ones shielded from sunlight were able to come back to life upon returning to Earth. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Who's really No. 1? Statisticians build a better way to make sense of competing sports rankings
item.description: Who, really, is the best player in baseball? Ask five sports media outlets and you may get five different answers. Rankings can vary dramatically from one source to another, change from year to year and leave out different players altogether, making it difficult to determine where there is genuine consensus and where opinions diverge. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Why are employees reluctant to disclose AI use to their bosses?
item.description: Countless employees across the country are experimenting with artificial intelligence (AI) to streamline workflows and increase productivity. Yet many are keeping these solutions to themselves. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Parking policy masks anti-Muslim discrimination for communities building new mosques
item.description: When the Islamic Society of Santa Barbara welcomed its community to its newly built mosque in 2019, nearly 19 years had passed since it purchased the property. The city's permitting process alone took 10 years. The project faced delays during 16 public hearings, at which residents of the suburban town of Goleta raised concerns, particularly about where worshippers would park their cars. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Invasive marine species set to take advantage of rising seas
item.description: More than two-thirds of newly flooded coastlines worldwide could become suitable habitat for 122 non-native marine species—including Chinese mitten crabs, Pacific oysters and Asian tiger shrimp—by the middle and end of this century. The research, published in Nature Ecology & Evolution, identifies coastal regions at heightened risk, including the eastern United States, the Gulf of Mexico, coastlines bordering the North Sea, southeastern China and northern Australia. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: More damaged trees mean fewer ecosystem benefits for low-income residents
item.description: Maya Mangala-Munuma '25 first noticed it in her hometown of Grand Rapids, Michigan. When she walked from an affluent neighborhood to a more impoverished one, it wasn't just the houses and demographics that changed. The trees did, too. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: To find a host cricket, this parasitic fly listens to more than the beat
item.description: A pregnant female Ormia ochracea fly has a challenging problem to solve. She must listen for the song of a male cricket, locate him in the dark and use him as a host for her developing offspring. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Megacohete Starship de SpaceX alcanza órbita terrestre por primera vez
item.description: 🚀 SpaceX lanzó este 28 de septiembre su gigantesco cohete Starship a órbita por primera vez, con el objetivo de completar seis vueltas a la Tierra para demostrar que está listo para el programa lunar Artemis de la NASA. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Coast redwoods slow their 'breathing' and 'eating' when temperatures spike
item.description: California's iconic coast redwoods are used to growing in cool, coastal areas where the average temperature is around 59 degrees F (15 degrees Celsius). But as average yearly temperatures rise and heat waves push temperatures above 100 degrees F (38 degrees Celsius), the trees are responding by slowing the very process that nourishes them, according to a study from the University of California, Davis. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Road testing: Research team studies potholes in quest for better asphalt sustainability
item.description: A Missouri S&T research team is studying asphalt binders, the materials that hold road materials together, to better understand how they perform and help improve the durability of Missouri's roads. Because roads are constantly exposed to sunlight, changing weather and the stress of daily traffic, these binders can break down over time, making reliable testing essential. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New tool tracks a hidden protein involved in viral infection and cell cleanup
item.description: Viruses such as influenza A and dengue can hijack a cellular system that helps manage protein aggregates. Previous work by FMI emeritus group leader Patrick Matthias and his team showed that a small protein called ubiquitin plays an important role in this process. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The Andes were supposed to stop this cacao killer. They didn't.
item.description: Black pod disease destroys up to a quarter of the world's cacao every year, roughly 700,000 metric tons worth more than $2 billion. The water mold responsible across the Americas is Phytophthora palmivora, and in Colombia it is the dominant Phytophthora on cacao. How it travels among the country's three Andean regions, though, has remained an open question. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA, Boeing Share Update on Commercial Starliner Development Plans
item.description: On Monday, NASA and Boeing provided an update on the company’s Starliner spacecraft, including adding additional crew missions and certifying a new rocket for crew transportation to low Earth orbit. “We are living through the most exciting era of space exploration since Apollo,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “As this domain continues to open, there […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Gerelle Q. Dodson

item.title: How to balance quantum batteries' high power with stable energy delivery
item.description: Quantum batteries are an emerging area of research, with progress coming from theoretical studies and proof-of-principle experiments in small quantum systems. Unlike conventional chemical batteries used in everyday life, they use quantum systems to store and transfer energy. Researchers are exploring them as potential future energy sources for quantum processors and other quantum technologies. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Armstrong Celebrates 80 Years of Flight Innovation
item.description: On Sept. 30, 1946, five National Advisory Committee of Aeronautics (NACA) engineers arrived at Muroc Army Airfield in California’s high desert to achieve supersonic flight for the first time. In less than two years, NACA flew the X-1 aircraft faster than the speed of sound, marking an important milestone in aviation history. Fast forward 80 […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Dede Dinius

item.title: Financial stress bleeds into our relationships. But partners who provide emotional support can help.
item.description: When a big credit card bill arrives or the rent is due, that stress can spill into our closest relationships, adding another source of tension between partners. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Shared DNA switch turns on genes in both bacteria and yeast
item.description: Microbial cell factories that produce pharmaceutical ingredients and other useful compounds include both the bacterium Escherichia coli and yeast, the organism used to leaven bread and ferment alcohol. The two organisms turn genes on by different rules, so a production design built for one has been hard to transfer to the other. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Online educational resources present imperialism in a positive light, involve students in inappropriate discussions
item.description: Teachers are increasingly turning from print textbooks to online materials to teach their courses. But when tasked with finding information online, they can encounter questionable or unreliable material. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Quantum computer boldly goes where no quantum computer has gone before: Space
item.description: There's big news from the quantum world. A quantum computer has been used in space for the first time. The device was aboard a spacecraft in low Earth orbit and demonstrated technology that could eventually help solve a problem that has been bugging satellites for years. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Social media may make investors feel more confident than they should be
item.description: Investment advice is only a scroll away. But new research from the University of Georgia suggests social media may leave some investors feeling more knowledgeable than they actually are. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Testing tiny telescope robots reveals design changes that could improve galaxy maps
item.description: Astronomers have cataloged billions of stars and hundreds of billions of galaxies. We have found thousands of planets orbiting stars. We can also map where galaxies sit and trace how the universe changes over time. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Childless women who shape history and culture are still judged on not being mothers
item.description: The women I return to most—Elizabeth I, her potential heir Arbella Stuart (and rival to James Charles Stuart, later King James I), Virginia Woolf, Katharine Hepburn, Debbie Harry—never had children. Their reasons were wildly different: some chose not to, some were prevented, and some never got the chance. The pattern raises two questions. Did their work or their position cost them their choice? And why does it seem to matter, overshadowing the legacies and achievements of great women? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Blue-light tools let researchers track, redirect and sever cells' transport routes
item.description: Light is fundamental to human life—without it, we'd be hungry, cold and blind. But what if the same light that sustains us could also be used to control and observe parts of cells within our bodies? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New model explains why glass becomes less transparent to terahertz light
item.description: Electromagnetic waves in the gigahertz (GHz) range, such as those used in mobile communications, can readily pass through many types of glass. However, transmission decreases significantly at terahertz frequencies above a characteristic threshold. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Highlights Lessons Learned From Swift Boost Mission
item.description: A commercial mission to boost NASA’s Swift observatory concluded without raising the spacecraft’s orbit, but the agency and industry vendor gained valuable experience that will benefit future in-space servicing programs. Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Scientists find lunar 'magnetic fossil' in Chang'e-6 samples
item.description: The moon no longer has a global magnetic field, but lunar rocks and soils still contain records of ancient magnetism. Studying the magnetic minerals in these samples can help scientists understand how the moon's magnetic field evolved over time. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Neuroproteins are potential diagnostic tool for sick foals
item.description: Researchers from North Carolina State University have found that blood serum concentrations of neuroproteins and neurosteroids are associated with neonatal maladjustment syndrome (NMS) in newborn foals. The work could lead to better diagnostic tools and potential therapies. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: SpaceX puts Starship megarocket in orbit for first time
item.description: SpaceX launched its enormous Starship into orbit for the first time on Monday and successfully delivered the most advanced Starlink satellites yet, but cut the flight short to ensure safety. The spacecraft re-entered over the Pacific and splashed down north of Hawaii three hours after blasting off from Texas. The company had been aiming for a 10-hour flight, spanning six full laps around Earth, to prove its readiness for Nasa’s Artemis moon programme. Starship tipped over and erupted in flames... item.title: The joy of song: Where songbirds came from and why we should listen to them
item.description: In 2001, I had an epiphany while making my first trip to Australia. Walking across a remote sheep station in the dusty west, my ears were suddenly filled with the rich, spirited song of three pied butcherbirds. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Halting plastic flows into oceans by 2050 may not stop microplastic buildup
item.description: Halting new marine plastic inputs by 2050 is the core objective of the Osaka Blue Ocean Vision, which was shared and endorsed alongside the G20 Implementation Framework for Actions on Marine Plastic Litter. However, stopping new plastic inputs will not remove existing marine debris, which can gradually fragment into microplastics that are difficult and costly to remove. Source reduction must therefore be accompanied by cleanup of legacy plastic debris. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Bullfrog brains can make their own backup fuel
item.description: For decades, scientists believed most animals relied on a steady supply of glucose, the body's primary fuel source, to power their brains. When glucose runs out, neural activity begins to fail, potentially leading to lasting brain damage. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: What's behind part-time work for men
item.description: In Switzerland, 40% of the working population works part-time, according to 2025 figures from the Federal Statistical Office (FSO). Women account for the lion's share: 60% of women in the workforce are employed part-time, while only more than 1 in 5 men work part-time. These figures place Switzerland second among the 38 countries of the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) in terms of part-time work, just behind the Netherlands. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Successful Earth flyby improves Juice’s course to Jupiter
item.description: The European Space Agency’s Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer ( Juice ) skimmed the very outer edge of Earth’s atmosphere on 28 September, using the gravity of our home planet to alter its route to Jupiter using very little fuel. Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.description: The NASA ORBIT (Opportunities in Research, Business, Innovation, and Technology for the Workforce) Challenge invites university and community college students nationwide to work with real NASA intellectual property and mission challenges. item.title: SpaceX’s Starship rocket reaches orbit for first time
item.description: SpaceX’s massive Starship rocket reached orbit for the first time on Monday morning, achieving a milestone for the programme after the mission briefly looked at risk because an engine failed during ascent. Starship took off at 7.49am local time out of SpaceX’s Starbase launch facility in South Texas, embarking on what could be a nearly 10-hour long test flight. The uncrewed 40-story-tall rocket was carrying 26 of the company’s upgraded Starlink satellites that SpaceX intended to deploy in orbit... Publicado también por: CNBC - World, ABC News Australia, MarketWatch, TechCrunch, The Times of India - World, Phys.org. Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.description: Starship no se parece demasiado a la imagen tradicional que tenemos de un cohete. Es una enorme mole de acero inoxidable de 124 metros de altura que SpaceX ha lanzado una y otra vez para probar, vuelo tras vuelo, cómo separar sus etapas, regresar desde el espacio y recuperar un sistema concebido para ser reutilizado. Esa barrera acaba de caer. El vuelo número 14 ha llevado por fin a la Ship 41 hasta… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: The right timing of treatment keeps resistant cells in check, yeast experiments suggest
item.description: The development of treatment resistance is one of the key challenges in modern cancer and antibiotic therapy. New therapeutic approaches aim to curb the spread of resistance through the targeted timing of treatment cycles. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Climate risks don't stop at sector boundaries—our responses shouldn't either
item.description: Australia's first mandatory climate reporting regime is now upon us. Since January 2025, organizations across the economy have been required to comply with AASB S2. It requires organizations to assess their climate risks and opportunities and show how they plan to stay resilient under plausible future climate scenarios. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: La nave alcanzó la órbita terrestre después de 13 intentos fallidos y dio un salto decisivo en el proyecto de SpaceX para revolucionar los lanzamientos y llevar astronautas a la Luna Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.

item.title: Worm experiments reveal how epigenetic effects persist across generations
item.description: Every cell in an organism contains the same DNA, which carries all the instructions needed for it to function. Yet cells do not all use the same genes: A nerve cell, for example, does not activate the same genes as a muscle cell. Epigenetics refers to the mechanisms that allow gene activity to be modulated without changing the DNA sequence. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA tests dual mode propulsion CubeSat ahead of launch
item.description: Spacecraft propulsion traditionally relies on volatile fuels and separate, bulky systems for different types of maneuvering in space. NASA is working to change that. Engineers at NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, recently completed a series of environmental and physical tests on a new small satellite designed to make spaceflight safer and more efficient. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: One of Canada's worst invasive species may have arrived naturally
item.description: Most invasive species are introduced into the areas where they become damaging. That's part of why they tend to be so successful in taking over new environments and causing billions of dollars in damage. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: A thunderous lift off, rapid satellite deployments and a fiery ending. That's how SpaceX's 14th launch of its Starship rocket panned out today. Fuente: BBC News - World.

item.title: Heat pump sales soar across Europe after states cut electricity taxes, data shows
item.description: EU to push member states to cut tax rate below duty on gas, with 11% surge in sales also put down to fallout from Iran war Business live – latest updates Europe live – latest updates Sales of residential heat pumps increased 11% across Europe in the first six months of the year as the Iran war sent oil and gas prices rocketing and some countries lowered electricity taxes. Homeowners bought 1.16m heat pumps across 12 European countries, up from 1.05m in the first half of 2025, according to the European Heat Pump Association (EHPA). Continue reading... item.title: Diabetes study finds keeping blood sugar too steady may come at a price
item.description: People with diabetes reported better quality of life after days when their glucose stayed largely within a healthy range, even when levels fluctuated more than usual. The unexpected finding suggests that pursuing extremely tight glucose control may sometimes come with a hidden lifestyle burden. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A tiny stellar system may be a 'satellite of a satellite'
item.description: Astronomers using data from the Euclid space telescope have discovered an exceptionally faint stellar system near the Fornax dwarf galaxy. Called Fornax-7, it appears to contain only about 170 times the mass of the sun in stars. The discovery paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Sept. 13. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: What role does high school play in mental health? Feeling connected to other students and staff is key
item.description: By age 15, an Australian student may have spent as many as 11,000 hours at school. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Mapping one atom's interaction with light uncovers an unbounded network of quantum states
item.description: A new graph-theoretic framework provides a unified description of atom-light interactions across regimes ranging from weak to deep-strong coupling. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists just discovered what coffee really does to your gut and brain
item.description: A new study suggests coffee may influence mood and brain function by changing the activity of microbes in the gut. Both caffeinated and decaf coffee were linked to lower stress, depression, and impulsivity, while also producing measurable changes in gut bacteria and metabolites. Decaf was associated with better learning and memory, while caffeinated coffee appeared to reduce anxiety and improve attention. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: 84 cents for every $1: Why indigenous workers earn less in Australia—and what to do about it
item.description: Indigenous workers in Australia earn 15.9% less per hour on average than all workers—or 84 cents for every $1 earned by non-Indigenous people—our research found. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Magnetic order survives weak quantum fluctuations in gapless magnets
item.description: In a new study published in Physical Review Letters, researchers have shown that magnetic order can survive weak quantum fluctuations in disordered magnets that lack an energy gap. The work establishes robust ferromagnetism in the two-dimensional random-bond quantum Ising model, confirming a longstanding conjecture in quantum statistical mechanics. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Zebrafish reveal wider role for gene linked to human albinism
item.description: Tiny, striped zebrafish are helping scientists trace how a gene linked to albinism influences eye development, work that may ultimately help explain some of the vision problems experienced by people with the condition and guide the search for new treatments. Fuente: Phys.org.
